She's concerned about grocery bills, future, and past. There’s no discipline or focus in her ideas—stream of consciousness, just like today’s thinking. In a world where God is dead, we can’t imagine a spiritual realm, only focusing on the present, leading to meaningless, insufficient lives with brains fixated on trivial matters.

All right? Does that make sense, guys? I have a question about forgiveness: if you can't forgive yourself, you can't forgive others. China hates Japan due to the war invasion, thinking it’s because China cannot forgive itself for being weak. Similarly, China can’t fight back and forgive Japan. 

So, my wife sends me YouTube comments as homework; I respond. Wes andQatara asked about Africa: interesting but I need more knowledge. I want to focus on Africa later and learn more about the continent.

A YouTuber named bad Bentham said livestock were the main currency for Step people, allowing them to fight great wars without logistical issues. Capital becomes utilitarian when hard work and motivation are saturated; we’re only moving in one direction. Societies collapse if they become too utilitarian.

This series is similar to Civilization series: using previous content to better understand history from different angles. Last year, I focused on how civilizations worked; this year, applying secret societies for a deeper understanding. Some content repeats, but the perspective has changed. Children give us hope and purpose in worsening times.
